subject: Energy
title: Conservation of Energy
description: A quick, practical guide to Conservation of Energy.

hook.text: Energy cannot be created or destroyed—only converted from one form to another. This is the first law.

buildup.text: When you turn on a lamp, electrical energy becomes light and heat—the total energy before and after is identical.

discovery.text: Emmy Noether proved in 1918 that energy conservation arises from time symmetry—physics works the same today as tomorrow.

twist.text: Even in nuclear reactions, energy is conserved—mass itself converts to energy via E=mc², but nothing is lost.

climax.text: The total energy of the universe has been constant since the Big Bang—about 13.8 billion years of perfect accounting.

punchline.text: The universe never loses a joule—it just moves them around.

quiz.question: What does time symmetry guarantee according to Noether?
